tip: Indonesian skips the 'it' in 'it's raining' – hujan is a verb on its own. Sedang marks in progress: sedang hujan deras = raining hard right now.
The -nya on cuacanya isn't 'its' here – it marks the weather as the known topic, like English 'the': cuacanya cerah = the weather is clear.
No perfect tense needed – sudah plus a time span covers 'has been': Sudah tiga hari hujan tidak berhenti = it's been three days of nonstop rain.
